title: Check at plan time that the design names the code it changes
summary: Add an early gate in the plan/reading step that refuses a design or plan entry which does not name the existing code (paths or symbols) it changes or reuses, so mismatches are caught before production rather than at the final verdict. Audience: the Athena maintainer. Overlap with the queued item reading-or-provenance-mismatch-caught-only-at-final-verdict is handled by implementing one shared early check and not duplicating it.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust under crates/.
New tests plus cargo test and clippy clean.
Tests assert the early refusal happens, not that types exist.
Gate moved to plan time, where the cause arises, not patched at the verdict.
One focused gate, shared with the overlapping queued item.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The plan gate lives in crates/athena-core (plan.rs PlanEntry::missing / reading.rs plan_entry); I did not read their bodies, so the producer must confirm the exact home.
'Names the existing code' means the design text cites at least one repository path that exists in the checkout, or states explicitly that it is wholly new code.
The root cause is that the named-code requirement was only checked by the verifier at the final verdict, never when the plan or design was written.

The queued item reading-or-provenance-mismatch-caught-only-at-final-verdict is the same root cause; the change should cover it where it can and the producer should record the overlap in the commit message and not close the other item.

acceptance_criteria.text: The commit message or code docs name the root cause: the design's code references were not checked until the final verdict, and say how the change overlaps with reading-or-provenance-mismatch-caught-only-at-final-verdict.

A new test feeds a plan entry or design that names no existing code, or names a path that does not exist, and asserts it is refused or flagged before production. It fails on the pre-change code and passes with the change. Run: cargo test.
A new test shows a design that names existing repository paths, or states that it is wholly new code, is accepted, so the gate is not a blanket refusal. Run: cargo test.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy (all targets, no warnings), and cargo test all pass.
The refusal message tells the author what is missing, e.g. which design names no existing code, in plain wording a stranger can follow.

out_of_scope: Closing or reworking the queued item reading-or-provenance-mismatch-caught-only-at-final-verdict beyond the shared check
Changing prompt files or the verifier's final-verdict logic
Editing records/ or the cited introspections
departures: Slightly lower acceptance: I could not confirm where the plan gate lives, and the overlap with the queued item is ambiguous.
urgent_reason: Moves a mismatch check from the final verdict to plan time, which cuts rejected attempts and redo-work retries.
hard_reason: Changes the plan gate that decides which jobs proceed to production, so a mistake could wrongly refuse or admit work.
